requirements.requirement: Identify the originating node, earliest relevant Loki timestamp, and initiating error using the existing node1 observability services.
requirements.summary: The Loki query directly shows the earliest INC-042 event at 1790945127292179581 on node2: nginx rejected the unknown `upstream_timeoutx` directive. Grafana and Loki were also directly observed healthy before remediation and after node1 recovery.

requirements.requirement: Correct the originating fault and restore catalog-api on node2:18081.
requirements.summary: The executor removed only the invalid directive, validated nginx, restarted it, and directly observed catalog-api healthy and listening. After a bounded node2 reboot, the boot identity changed and configuration validation, listener, catalog response, and data hashes all recovered.

requirements.requirement: Restore orders-api on node3:18082, checkout-api on node4:18083, and the complete request path from node1.
requirements.summary: Direct checks show active nginx listeners and successful dependency-chain responses at all three tiers, followed by a successful node1-to-node4-to-node3-to-node2 request. Serial node4, node3, node2, and node1 reboots each produced a new boot identity and successful post-restart path checks; the final node1 check confirmed the complete path after all restarts.

requirements.requirement: Record the originating node, earliest relevant Loki timestamp, and initiating error in /root/INC-042-report.txt on node1.
requirements.summary: The required root-owned report was created with node2, the correct nanosecond Loki timestamp and UTC rendering, and the nginx initiating error. Its contents and restrictive mode were directly rechecked after node1 reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve incident history, catalog data, and unrelated service configuration.
requirements.summary: Catalog hashes match the prepared baseline before remediation and after node2 reboot. All three original Loki events remain queryable after node1 reboot. The complete audited timeline shows only the targeted removal of the invalid nginx line, creation of the required report, service restart, and mandatory node reboots; lifecycle observations show healthy packages, no failed services, and only the intended listeners afterward.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Loki directly identifies node2's invalid nginx directive as the initiating fault; the targeted correction restored all three tiers and the complete request path; the required incident report exists; and incident history and catalog data were preserved. The provider-wide restart protocol is strong for all four nodes: each has pre-restart health and boot identity, an acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity corroborated by fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered service and end-to-end state.
limitations: Preservation of unrelated configuration is supported by the complete audited command trace and lifecycle health observations rather than exhaustive before-and-after hashes of every unrelated configuration file.

The node2 configuration edit and nginx restart directly corrected the originating fault (cmd-152566b9d9554ac7); the node1 file write created the contractually required report (cmd-093c9a969cef4c48); and the four reboot commands implemented the mandatory restart-evidence protocol (cmd-4a11c7e18b844c37, cmd-c6dcae306a7f4b70, cmd-0cc4c89005754858, cmd-86ecb763c07b4c0d). The reboot log files were bounded temporary artifacts and are absent from the final temporary-file inventories.
